title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used a declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces were recorded and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, expanded interpretation of discordant outcomes and failure modes grounded in execution traces, clarify execution semantics, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A practical safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and incurring interaction costs [see evidence synthesis]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes.

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. Verifier-guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics, so we used deterministic controlled faults that guarantee activation in a paired design that reuses the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair architectures have been studied across code, IaC, and DSL settings. Prior controlled evaluations show that interposing deterministic verifiers between stochastic generation and acceptance increases verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model raises the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck. Complementary work documents caveats: single-proxy verifier loops can be exploited (optimization toward the proxy) and verifier mediation imposes measurable interaction/compute overheads (the verifier tax). Survey and field studies for NetOps emphasize that LLMs help with read-oriented tasks but provide weaker guarantees for safe closed-loop changes without conservative orchestration. The supplied evidence synthesis summarizes these findings, highlights gaps in direct vendor-CLI experimental coverage, and motivates a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that (a) forces initial-intervention activation via deterministic fault injection, (b) reuses a shared controlled-fault candidate across paired arms to isolate diagnostics exposure, and (c) archives validator traces sufficient for independent safety-statistic recomputation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success indicator requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Adapter and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of validator diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. Because the same initial sampled candidate and matched repair budget are shared across arms, observed differences isolate the effect of exposing validator diagnostics under the adapter contract. (Per the execution manifest, temperature is recorded as null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.)

Controlled-challenge bank, instrumentation, and scoring. The confirmatory bank consisted of 40 preregistered task indices populated by a deterministic fault injector that produced actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, unintended_state_change). The primary success predicate required agreement between the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. Per-episode validator traces, the frozen harmful-change labeling mapping (an episode is harmful if post-repair validation contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE), and all scored artifacts were recorded in the archive to enable deterministic independent recomputation of preregistered secondary safety aggregations. The preregistered stopping, exclusion, and missingness rules were followed (primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary').

Execution and statistical plan. Confirmatory execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= planned maximum 120). The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts, the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Sensitivity analyses treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118. Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507. Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729).

Missingness and preregistered safety aggregation status. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were recorded. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces required to compute it were recorded and permit deterministic reaggregation by independent auditors.

Representative example traces and diagnostic role. Representative archived scoring artifacts (task-000001..task-000003) illustrate how diagnostics change repair outcomes. Task-000001: baseline and guarded both started from the same shared_controlled_fault_candidate that triggered a FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH diagnostic; guarded received validator feedback and produced a corrected ordering that restored the required restore command (validation_after.valid = true), whereas baseline also reached valid outcome in this instance (n11 example). Task-000002: the shared candidate produced PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE violations in the baseline repair; under guarded the validator diagnostics were exposed, and the guarded repair avoided the protected-interface edit and achieved a valid configuration (an n10 case). Task-000003: baseline produced a post-repair PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and failed validation (score = 0), while the guarded repair (validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true) produced a valid post-repair configuration (an n10 case). These example traces demonstrate the concrete mechanism by which exposed violation codes (e.g., PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) can produce targeted corrective edits.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the primary contrast and discordant structure. The paired design and shared initial candidate semantics isolate diagnostic exposure as the treatment: both arms received the same sampled source candidate and identical repair-call budgets, so the observed differences (n10 = 9, n01 = 1) reflect how supplying deterministic validator diagnostics to the repair model changes repair behavior under matched upstream conditions. The observed pattern—nine tasks rescued by diagnostics versus a single task where baseline succeeded but guarded did not—makes the net improvement largely attributable to targeted avoidance or repair of validator-flagged violations rather than improved first-pass generation.

Mechanistic diagnostics and failure modes. Archived validator traces show recurrent diagnostic codes driving repairs: FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH (missing required restore), PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE (edits touching protected interfaces), and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE (edits modifying fields outside permitted workflows). In guarded episodes validator_trace.violation_codes were frequently present before repair and absent after guarded repair when success was achieved. These traces provide concrete evidence of the repair mechanism: diagnostics expose exact violation categories and sometimes line-level metadata (e.g., affected_interface), enabling focused corrective edits (reorder, add restore command, or remove protected edits) rather than broad rewriting. Representative artifacts substantiate these mechanism claims without inventing new measurements.

Difficulty composition and subgroup caution. The preregistered task bank includes tasks marked medium, hard, and very_hard in the archived task manifest; representative artifacts shown (task-000001..task-000006) span medium→very_hard patterns. Although diagnostics appear helpful across example difficulty patterns, complete_pairs = 39 limits statistical power for reliable per-difficulty confirmatory inference; per-fault-class comparisons are exploratory and were not preregistered as confirmatory. Any subgroup claims therefore remain provisional and require larger confirmatory replications.

Uncertainty, power, and ceiling effects. The primary paired bootstrap CI [0.0769, 0.3590] indicates that the true absolute guarded − baseline difference is plausibly in a range consistent with a meaningful operational improvement but smaller than the initially targeted ~30 percentage points used in the planning power heuristics. The observed discordant counts (n10 = 9, n01 = 1) produced sufficient evidence to reject the two-sided null at alpha = 0.05 in this confirmatory run, but the finite sample and the single-model, synthetic-bench scope caution against extrapolating magnitude or operational feasibility beyond the tested regime.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved verifier+simulator-validated success on this controlled bank, but verifier-guided workflows impose extra model–verifier interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls. These counts are archived and permit exploratory cost-per-avoided-failure calculations, but large-scale deployment assessments of latency, operator triage cost, and orchestration complexity require broader studies. The verified evidence supports framing reduced residual verifier-detected failures as an empirical outcome within the synthetic controlled challenge, not as a proven operational win in heterogeneous production environments.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation (bounded increase threshold) was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary; consequently no confirmatory safety verdict is claimed here. The frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces were recorded and provide exact inputs for deterministic recomputation; until recomputation is shown within a confirmatory artifact, any harmful-overrepair numbers remain exploratory.

Verifier-exploitation and mitigations. Prior work documents verifier-exploitation risk when single-proxy verifiers are iteratively optimized. The short-horizon repair budget and shared-candidate pairing used here reduce exposure to long-horizon exploitation, but the risk remains for longer agentic pipelines. The archived artifacts show single-step corrections rather than multi-step agentic edits; proposed mitigations (multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints, calibrated abstention) are presented as hypotheses and design options rather than empirical findings in this execution.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation effects; differences across arms reflect diagnostics exposure under the adapter contract. Construct validity: primary success required agreement of a deterministic validator and a simulator; both components constrain the operational meaning of “valid.” External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank, restricting generalization to diverse vendor equipment and live operator streams. Conclusion validity: the sample (complete_pairs = 39) yields a statistically detectable effect for the observed discordant structure but limits precision for subgroup inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). Mechanistic evidence in archived validator traces shows that diagnostics frequently expose concise violation codes (e.g., PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and metadata that appear to enable targeted corrective edits, accounting for most discordant rescued cases. The finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications, larger sample sizes for per-fault-class inference, and deployment-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
